findings.title: SimCore._pick_next_pipe crashes on empty routes (typed nil assignment) - the no_route contract is unpinnable and its new test aborts with 3 phantom checks
findings.detail: R1 W5's recommended fold crashes the sim instead of pinning the invariant: 3 of the 5 new isolation checks are phantom. Game demand is guarded by _reachable (null-safe untyped local) so runtime play never hits it - but the harness door _spawn_packet (documented staging door) hard-crashes on any zero-pipe spawn.
findings.recommended_fix: Untype the local (var r = routes.get(dst), matching _reachable's pattern) or routes.get(dst, {}); then re-run the suite and confirm the 3 phantom checks now execute and pass (add drops.is_empty() branch-guard first).

findings.title: run_tests.gd abort guard is ineffective for real abort semantics - suite printed PASS (0 failures) over a crashed test with 3 checks never executed
findings.detail: The claimed W10 fold checks for a null result, but on Godot 4.7.1 an aborted awaited coroutine yields an int (r1's own reproduction documented this); the is-int guard passes it through. The A1 exit-0 gate false-greens over exactly the abort class it was folded to catch.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the guard semantic, not type-based: have each test's run_all bump a suite-level expected-check counter that run_tests compares against printed oks per script (any shortfall = FAIL), or count check() invocations via a shared counter and fail on under-delivery; additionally guard array-tail derefs in tests so aborts convert to counted failures.

findings.title: main._ready still computes wedge_layout twice while _generate_world's docstring promises 'computed ONCE by the caller and threaded through' (N24 fold overclaims)
findings.evidence:
_generate_world(WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED))
	sim = SimCore.new()
	sim.setup(SEED, WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED)))
--- vs docstring: 'The layout is computed ONCE by the caller and threaded through, so staged nodes and sim placements can never drift onto different layouts.'
findings.detail: The fold threaded layout into _generate_world but sim.setup independently recomputes wedge_layout(SEED). Pure SEED function so results are identical (no drift), but the newly-added 'ONCE' invariant is factually false - doc overclaim introduced by the fix itself.
findings.recommended_fix: Compute var layout := WorldSeed.wedge_layout(SEED) once in _ready; pass it to both _generate_world(layout) and WorldSeed.node_placements(SEED, layout).

findings.evidence: sim_core.gd:384: 'pkt.progress_milli = int(pkt.progress_milli) + SimBalance.LANE_SPEED_MILLI[int(pkt.lane)]'; sim_balance.gd:54: 'const LANE_SPEED_MILLI := [200, 100, 60] # travel milli-units per tick, by lane (speed = priority)'. grep over tests/ for LANE_SPEED_MILLI / lane-speed pins: zero matches.

findings.title: ECMP uses chained WorldSeed.hash_i32 (murmur-style 32-bit finalizer), GDD M3 canon names splitmix64(src, dst, class, pkt_id) mod N
findings.evidence: GDD M3 (gdd.md:166): 'deterministic ECMP hash `splitmix64(src, dst, class, pkt_id) mod N`'; code: 'var h := WorldSeed.hash_i32(WorldSeed.hash_i32(...))' where hash_i32 is a 2-round 0x45D9F3B 32-bit avalanche (world_seed.gd:30-34), not splitmix64.
findings.detail: Determinism contract fully holds (pure, replay-stable, pinned); the named algorithm differs from canon text. Distribution quality of a 2-round 32-bit chain over 4 fields is weaker than splitmix64 but unproven problematic at this scale.
findings.recommended_fix: Either note the substitution in the GDD/code comment, or switch to a splitmix64 implementation for the ECMP stream and re-pin.

findings.detail: Label overclaim only; the pin still proves regeneration determinism+idempotence. Was note-level in r1; fold didn't touch it.
findings.recommended_fix: Compare exactly (==) or reword the message/docblock to 'approximately identical'.

findings.title: Deactivation 'still flows' check is polluted by natural demand (delivered+dropped >= QUEUE_DEPTH over 1800 ticks passes even if the stranded six vanish)
findings.detail: Natural demand delivers hundreds over 1800 ticks; the stranded-cohort accounting is not cohort-scoped, so silent stranding of the six would not flip it.
findings.recommended_fix: Scope to the cohort: capture the stranded ids before deactivation and assert each is delivered or dropped by id.

findings.title: test_sim_flow header claims 'natural demand cannot pollute the pins' but the delivered-count pins count sim-wide
findings.evidence: ## origin-destination pair so natural demand cannot pollute the pins. ... check(int(r1.sim.sla["email"].delivered) > 30, "ECMP diamond delivers (...)") [sla counts include natural demand]
findings.detail: The OD-filter (_od_inflight) does isolate the routing pins; the delivered>30 thresholds are sim-wide so natural demand contributes. Claim is broader than the mechanism.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword the header to name which pins are OD-scoped, or count via the OD inflight sets.

findings.title: Serialization wave-2 ordering check passes vacuously if the wave-1 email already left (find(email_id) == -1 makes the ordering compare trivially true)
findings.evidence: check(int(inflight2[inflight2.size() - 1]) == be_id and inflight2.find(be_id) > inflight2.find(email_id), "serialization: Best-effort admits after the higher lanes ...")
findings.detail: Only the tail==be_id half does unconditional work; the ordering half depends on email_id still being in-flight.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard: if not inflight2.has(email_id): skip the ordering compare with an explicit weaker assertion (or spawn fresh waves).

findings.title: set_lanes per-value bounds branch (negative or >100 share with total <= 100) untested
findings.detail: One validation branch without a negative leg; minor gap in an otherwise well-pinned bus.
findings.recommended_fix: Add [-10, 55, 55] and [50, 60, -10] legs asserting no-op + recording.

findings.title: Alloc-change rebuild (strand re-thickening), MAX_DOTS ghost-guard, and reversed b->a dot rendering remain unasserted (capture-backed per A2)
findings.evidence: elif meta.get("alloc", []) != p.alloc: _rebuild_view(id, p) [no test asserts strand thickness changes] ... if used >= MAX_DOTS_PER_PIPE: ... capped = true
findings.detail: P3 visual surfaces verified via captures 06/07 per epic A2 doctrine; strand_point/sample_at geometry IS now pinned (_strand_geometry).
findings.recommended_fix: Optional light pins: set_lanes then assert arc rebuilt shares; flood > 48 and assert visible dot count caps.

findings.title: Latency breach events now carry pipe/node (W7 fix verified in code) but no pin asserts the attribution fields
findings.evidence: check(int(s.lat_tick) >= 0 and not (s.events as Array).is_empty(), "SLA: breach carries tick + event record") - does not inspect events[0].pipe/node.
findings.detail: The A1 'attributable' contract for latency is implemented but unpinned; a regression back to -1/-1 would pass.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the check: assert the latency event's pipe >= 0 and node >= 0.

findings.title: _regenerate_preview (the button body) is never executed by tests - the suite replicates its two calls directly (downgraded from warning)
findings.detail: The guarded handler cannot execute headless by design; its body pieces are individually pinned and the @export_tool_button wiring is structurally asserted. Residual risk: handler drift vs replicated body. P3.
findings.recommended_fix: If desired, drive it via Engine physics in an editor-hint simulation, or assert the handler's source contains exactly the two tested calls.
